Check out this shot of Phobos, the larger of Mars's two little moons! It looks like a lumpy potato, and honestly, that's pretty much what it is. It's only about 22 kilometers across, which means its gravity is too weak to pull it into a ball. See those grooves running across the surface? Scientists think they may be cracks caused by tidal stress from Mars, or maybe leftover marks from a big impact. And the giant crater on one end is called Stickney; it's so large that the impact almost broke the moon apart. Phobos is also sinking, slowly, toward Mars. In about 50 million years it'll either crash into the planet or break up into a ring.
